    "summary": "[GOAL] Auto-compact fragile-band escalation — one deepening pass when thin relief leaves hides exhausted",
    "description": "**[WIP][GOAL] Auto-compact fragile-band escalation — after any automatic structured run settles with less than one full reserve of headroom, perform exactly one bounded checkpoint deepening pass, whether or not hideable entries remain**

## Goal (v2 — review findings incorporated)

One sentence: **an automatic structured compaction that only just ducks under the trigger must not immediately re-enter the same expensive ladder — when its settled headroom is smaller than `settings.reserveTokens`, it performs exactly one additional structured checkpoint pass, while healthy/deep results and all forced-run semantics remain unchanged.**

This is a relief-quality fix, not a judge-timeout fix. The repeated 2×300 s judge stalls are a separate degraded-endpoint problem; this card reduces how quickly a thin result leads back to that ladder. A judge circuit breaker/cooldown is explicit follow-up work.

## Incident and numeric contract

Session sid `01a17c9c`, late Oct 2026, window 400,000 tokens (`contextWindow` override), smol role `glm-5.3-flash @ api.z.ai`.

`~/.fah/logs/fa.log` showed repeated hide-judge timeouts followed by deterministic hides:

```text
auto-compact start tokens=385619
auto-compact pass 2 FAILED — hide judge failed call / timeout (300 s)
hide-fallback tokens 385619→360497 ok=true
…next fire…
auto-compact pass 2 FAILED — hide judge failed call / timeout (300 s)
hide-fallback tokens 375609→360010 ok=true
…next fire…
auto-compact pass 1 local-trim tokens 360010→63268
```

A manual `/compact` subsequently cut approximately 354k→48k. Each automatic degraded fire could burn two judge attempts and still leave little headroom, so the next turn or two crossed the trigger again.

For a 400,000-token window, gh-1742 settings give:

```text
reserveTokens = 25,000
trigger       = 375,000
band          = reserveTokens = 25,000
```

The v1 review exposed why `reserveTokens ~/ 2` was wrong. The shipped predicate must cover the actual incident:

| Settled tokens | `margin = trigger − tokensAfter` | `< reserveTokens` (v2) | `< reserveTokens ~/ 2` (rejected v1) |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 360,497 | 14,503 | **escalate** | no |
| 360,010 | 14,990 | **escalate** | no |
| 354,000 | 21,000 | **escalate** | no |

Therefore v2 uses **strictly `margin < settings.reserveTokens`**, with no new configuration key.

## Verified mechanism (current code)

- **F1 — The pass loops stop at the trigger.** `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart`: `_runHidePasses` returns when `before <= trigger` (:395); `_runCheckpointPasses` uses the same gate (:603). `run()` computes `trigger = window − settings.reserveTokens` and finally returns `_requestTokens() <= trigger`.
- **F2 — Settings scale with the window.** `CompactionSettings.forWindow` (`lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart` :463+) derives reserve/keepRecent from the window. At 400k: reserve 25,000, keepRecent 50,000. The band must derive from `settings.reserveTokens`, never a hard-coded incident constant.
- **F3 — Deterministic hide is intentionally minimal.** `_deterministicHide` stops when `freed >= over` (:516). It does **not** scan to exhaustion and does **not** prove that no hideable entries remain.
- **F4 — A thin result does not imply hides are exhausted.** After a successful fallback hide, `_runHidePasses` can return on under-trigger before evaluating remaining candidates. Consequently `hides exhausted` is not a valid required escalation gate; it is diagnostic state only.
- **F5 — The hide judge receives the full visible-ledger render.** `_callJudge` calls `judge(view.ledger.render())` under the per-attempt budget. Two consecutive failures select `_deterministicHide`. This explains the expensive degraded path, but changing judge payload/budget/circuit-breaking is outside this card.
- **F6 — Checkpoint passes are the structured deepening mechanism.** They consolidate the oldest projected prefix outside the keepRecent tail, hide included markers at marker cost, respect pins/protected-tail/pair integrity, and chunk payloads to the summarizer window (#729). One checkpoint pass may make several chunked summarizer calls.
- **F7 — Forced and automatic structured success differ at the factory.** `AutoCompactorFactory.run` returns structured success when `outcome.ok && adapter.passCount > 0`, including forced runs. Classic fall-through is not a generic “forced runs always deepen” mechanism. Escalation in this card therefore applies only when the engine was entered with `force == false`; manual force and message-cap-forced semantics stay unchanged.

## Retracted alternatives

- **Fatter deterministic hide:** rejected. It violates #148 minimal-relief semantics; deepening is a separate checkpoint pass.
- **Require `_hideableEntries(...).isEmpty`:** rejected. Minimal fallback does not establish exhaustion and this gate misses the target incident.
- **Half-reserve band:** rejected numerically; it misses every quoted incident result.
- **Predict future growth/re-crossing:** rejected. Evaluate the settled result directly, following the #1914 detected-not-predicted discipline.
- **Classic-engine fallback inside `StructuredCompactor`:** rejected layering. The structured engine does not own `AutoCompactorFactory.build()`; any factory-level classic fallback requires a separate contract/card.
- **Config-only remedy:** smol-role and judge-budget settings are operational mitigations, not a mechanism fix.

## Design

Add one post-ladder checkpoint escalation inside `StructuredCompactor.run`, before the final verdict:

```text
run(force)
 ├─ existing pre-flight / LRU re-hide / hide / checkpoint ladder — unchanged
 ├─ if force == false:
 │    tokensAfter = _requestTokens()             // same basis as verdict
 │    margin      = trigger − tokensAfter
 │    if 0 <= margin && margin < settings.reserveTokens:
 │       perform AT MOST ONE checkpoint escalation pass
 └─ return _requestTokens() <= trigger           // verdict rule unchanged
```

### Exact escalation semantics

1. **One pass, not one LLM call.** Select one checkpoint range and process it through the existing checkpoint machinery. A chunked range may require multiple summarizer calls; all are part of the same escalation pass.
2. **No hideable-entries precondition.** Thin settled headroom is sufficient evidence. Hideable entries may remain; escalation must still fire.
3. **Automatic runs only.** `force == true` skips escalation. Since message-cap forcing reaches the engine as `force: force || capTriggered`, cap-forced runs also retain their existing behavior. The normal automatic token-pressure path has `force == false`.
4. **Existing checkpoint limits remain authoritative.** `maxCheckpointPasses == 0` disables the escalation. Otherwise escalation adds exactly one pass beyond the ordinary ladder. It never re-enters hide passes and never loops because the result is still thin.
5. **No foldable range is a bounded no-op.** If `_pickCheckpointRange()` returns null (including an entirely pinned/exempt foldable prefix), emit one unsuccessful/no-work escalation report and keep the existing verdict; do not fall through to classic compaction.
6. **Failure safety.** If the pass cannot produce/append a checkpoint, the pre-escalation result is retained. A previously under-trigger success is not flipped to failure merely because optional deepening failed.
7. **Cancellation and budget expiry are not ordinary optional-pass failure.** User/run cancellation preserves cancellation. Factory total-budget timeout retains the existing #515/#1425 outcome path; escalation must not start another attempt after budget exhaustion or append additional late work after the authoritative timeout outcome.
8. **Projection invariants are inherited, not reimplemented.** Protected tail, pins, whole-pair groups, keepRecent, depth-cap flattening, marker consolidation and expandability behave exactly as in an ordinary checkpoint pass.
9. **Marker-only ranges remain deterministic.** Existing marker-consolidation behavior is reused; no fake LLM/judge call is reported and no repeated range loop is introduced.

### Observability

- Add pass kind **`checkpoint-escalation`** to `StructuredCompactionPass.kind` and surface it through existing `onPass` → host reporting (#1636).
- The pass/report identifies the triggering `marginTokens` and `bandTokens` (existing report models may carry these as optional metadata; no breaking change).
- Emit one diagnostic line containing counts only: settled tokens, margin, band, remaining hideable-entry count, and outcome. **Never include rendered ledger/message content.**
- Escalation metrics/cooldown across separate runs are follow-up work, not hidden state in v2.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Incident-shaped thin relief escalates.** With `force == false`, settled margins 14,503 / 14,990 / 21,000 at the 400k settings each cause exactly one checkpoint escalation. No hideable-exhaustion condition is required.
- **AC2 — Deep/healthy results are unchanged.** `margin >= settings.reserveTokens` performs no escalation, adds no pass record/log line, and preserves existing run results/reporting byte-for-byte where no other changed behavior is involved.
- **AC3 — Remaining hideables do not suppress escalation.** A thin result with one or more `_hideableEntries` remaining still escalates exactly once (regression against rejected v1).
- **AC4 — Exact boundaries.** `margin == 0` escalates; `0 < margin < reserveTokens` escalates; `margin == reserveTokens` and larger do not; `margin < 0` is not treated as a successful thin settlement and does not enter this success-side escalation path.
- **AC5 — Automatic-only gating.** Manual `force == true` and cap-forced runs do not escalate; ordinary automatic runs do. Existing gh-1742 invariant-1/factory behavior remains unchanged.
- **AC6 — Bounded work.** At most one escalation per `run()`; no hide-pass re-entry and no second escalation even when the pass leaves a thin margin. `maxCheckpointPasses == 0` produces no checkpoint call/append.
- **AC7 — Failure/no-work preserves verdict.** Empty range, empty summary, or append/processing failure leaves the pre-escalation under-trigger success standing and emits an explicit no-work/failed escalation report.
- **AC8 — Existing checkpoint safety holds.** Protected-tail ids, pins, pair integrity, keepRecent, depth-cap and expandable checkpoint coverage are preserved; marker-only ranges make no LLM call.
- **AC9 — Chunking and time budget are honest.** A test with multiple chunks proves they belong to one escalation pass; per-call `attemptBudget` applies to each call, while the factory `totalBudget` remains the overall bound. No new attempt starts after total-budget exhaustion.
- **AC10 — Cancellation is preserved.** Run/user cancellation during escalation follows existing cancellation semantics and is not swallowed into “optional escalation failed, success stands.”
- **AC11 — Observability is content-safe.** `checkpoint-escalation` reaches host reporting with margin/band/outcome; diagnostic output has counts only and no ledger content.
- **AC12 — Incident regression.** Replay-shaped tests for 385,619→360,497 and 375,609→360,010 now escalate on the same run. The next run starting under trigger performs no judge call and no escalation; no third judge-stall is required to obtain deeper relief.
- **AC13 — Existing suites remain green.** #148/#287/#387/#388/#515/#541/#729/#1379/#1409/#1425/#1742 regression suites pass; golden healthy-run reports do not drift.

## Test plan

### Unit

- `UT-ESC-1/2/3` — all three incident margins escalate; deep relief does not; hideables-remaining does not suppress escalation.
- `UT-ESC-4` — boundary table: negative, zero, `reserve−1`, `reserve`, `reserve+1` margins.
- `UT-ESC-5` — `force` and cap-forced matrix; no escalation on either forced channel.
- `UT-ESC-6` — exactly one pass; still-thin result does not loop; zero checkpoint-pass limit respected.
- `UT-ESC-7` — null range / empty summary / failed processing preserve verdict and report no-work/failure.
- `UT-ESC-8` — pins, protected tail, pair groups, keepRecent, depth cap and marker-only range.
- `UT-ESC-9` — cancellation is rethrown/propagated according to existing contracts.
- `UT-ESC-10` — pass kind/report/log metadata and content-safety.

### Integration

- `IT-ESC-1` — fake judge fails twice → deterministic hide lands at 360,497-equivalent → same run performs checkpoint escalation without requiring hides exhausted.
- `IT-ESC-2` — multi-chunk checkpoint: N summarizer calls, one escalation record; timeout on chunk K follows existing budget semantics and starts no chunk K+1.
- `IT-ESC-3` — host report contains the escalation kind and numeric reason; no rendered transcript in logs.
- `IT-ESC-4` — post-escalation under-trigger run performs no pre-flight work; repeated separate runs never share hidden escalation state.
- `IT-ESC-5` — provider-usage/rebuilt-estimate fixture: predicate and final verdict use the same `_requestTokens()` basis after refresh.

### Regression / merge rule

- `REG-ESC-1` — healthy deep-relief, ordinary forced, cap-forced and classic-fall-through goldens remain unchanged.
- `REG-ESC-2` — the two quoted incident transitions are merge-blocking fixtures; a fix that does not escalate both cannot merge even if generic escalation tests pass.
- Run the full compaction/auto-compactor suites, `dart analyze`, loc/CRAP/jscpd gates; cover all new branches (>90% target for new code, repository hard ratchet unchanged).

## Additional border cases

- Very small windows: band derives from scaled settings; no fixed 25k assumption and no escalation when the result is already at least one reserve below trigger.
- All foldable records pinned or protected: bounded no-op, no classic/lossy escape.
- Huge protected tail leaving little foldable prefix: no pair splitting or tail violation to manufacture relief.
- One checkpoint consumes several chunks on a slow smol endpoint: existing total budget remains authoritative; this card does not promise “one 300-second budget.”
- Escalation leaves tokens above trigger or still in the band: no second pass in that run; final verdict follows existing logic.
- Concurrent session/kill/resume during compaction: existing session and #1425 recovery behavior remains authoritative; no new resume protocol.

## Non-goals

- No change to deterministic-hide relief or #148 minimal-relief semantics.
- No judge payload cap, timeout retuning, circuit breaker, cross-run cooldown, or smol-role selection changes.
- No classic-engine escalation/fall-through from the structured engine.
- No change to trigger math, LRU re-hide, local-trim valve, manual `/compact`, message-cap forcing, or gh-1742 invariant 1.
- No new config keys, growth prediction, checkpoint quality rewrite, or changes to pins/protected-tail rules.

## Decisions after review (no open questions)

- **Band:** `margin < settings.reserveTokens`, strict `<`; half-reserve is rejected by incident data.
- **Second gate:** none. `hides exhausted` is diagnostic only; minimal hide cannot prove it.
- **Deepening mechanism:** existing structured checkpoint machinery only; no classic fallback in this card.
- **Scope:** automatic token-pressure runs only (`force == false`).
- **Metric/pass name:** `checkpoint-escalation`.
- **Time bound:** existing per-call attemptBudget plus factory totalBudget; one pass is not one LLM call.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-2044): the auto-compact fragile-band escalation could fold the
  ENTIRE visible projection when the remaining path fit inside
  `keepRecentTokens` — the keep-recent walk defaulted to folding
  everything when its budget never exhausted, swallowing the live tail
  (the newest user ask and assistant turn included). Real-world trigger:
  resumed subagent runs ended with no assistant message at all
  (`subagent produced no assistant message` — CI cores shards 1/4 and
  3/4, hostile-env, both red). `_pickCheckpointRange` now declines the
  fold when the whole foldable path fits the keep-recent region and
  still carries live records; all-marker paths keep the lossless
  deterministic consolidation (issue #387). The escalation receipt also
  reports the REAL summarizer call count (a #729 chunked fold makes N
  calls, not 1), and the factory wires its run token into the engine's
  `cancelToken` so a watchdog-shaped cancel reason (any
  `TimeoutException`) can no longer dissolve a user abort into a
  "summarizer returned no text" failed receipt while the run reports
  success (#1085).

- fix(gh-2003): the Copilot picker filter is tier-aware. Individual-tier
  `/models` responses omit `model_picker_enabled` entirely, so phase 1
  dropped every such entry as «picker flag absent» and individual/OAuth
  accounts still listed zero usable models. When the response comes from
  the individual tier — the individual host (`api.githubcopilot.com` or
  pi-mono's `api.individual.githubcopilot.com` spelling) or a
  no-proxy-ep token (individual by design) — an ABSENT flag is now

  `cancelToken` so a watchdog-shaped cancel reason (any
  `TimeoutException`) can no longer dissolve a user abort into a
  "summarizer returned no text" failed receipt while the run reports
  success (#1085). Follow-up CI red on the same branch: the decline
  moved tiny-transcript runs to the classic residual engine, where an
  EMPTY summarizable region folded zero #729 chunks into a blank
  summary that still landed as a junk CompactionRecord and a hollow
  `success: true` through the no-work terminal — `compactSession` now
  refuses that empty-region blank fold (gh-1743's failure-verdict
  contract kept; a dialed blank answer over a real region still lands
  as a record, issue #578 unchanged).

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly

# gh-2044 rework — CI red fixed: the classic engine's hollow fold can no longer flip a failure verdict

## Issues/Notes

- **Open review threads: 0.** The GraphQL census in `pr_discussions_raw.json` shows 4 review threads, 0 unresolved — the four earlier threads (`dart format` clean, no-foldable-range coverage, `cancelToken: runToken` wiring, real `judgeCalls` counts) are resolved and their fixes verified on this head. `outputs/review_replies.json` therefore carries an empty reply list.

No owned-violations table exists to itemize; the red is accounted below as an owned regression of this PR (green on `origin/main`, red on the branch, root cause inside code this PR changed).
- Local SDK note: `dart format --output=none lib/ test/` still lists pre-existing formatter-drift files this PR does not touch (42 files, unchanged from the previous leg's audit) — left untouched deliberately to keep the diff surgical.

### The red (owned)

`test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart` — *"gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict"* asserted `ok == false` and got `true` (both CI jobs and a local repro). Root cause chain — every link inside this PR's scope:

1. This PR's keep-recent decline in `_pickCheckpointRange` (the correct whole-world-fold fix) makes the structured ladder **decline** the fold when the whole visible path fits `keepRecentTokens` — for the fixture (window 100, one ~10-token message) the structured engine does zero LM calls and settles `(ok: false, timedOut: false)`.
2. The factory's residual fall-through (#148 S7/D4) hands the run to the **classic** engine.
3. The classic engine folds an **empty summarizable region**: `generateSummary`'s #729 chunked path plans **zero chunks** and returns `''` without any LM call — `compactSession` used to append that blank summary as a **junk `CompactionRecord`** anyway.
4. Pass 2 then sees "last entry is already a compaction" → the no-work terminal returns `success: true` **unconditionally** — a hollow success while the context is still over the trigger (10 → 37 tokens, endpoint never dialed). gh-1743's failure-verdict contract was flipped into a fake success.

## Approach (TDD)

- **RED** — reproduced locally before touching production code: the failing test exits 1 with `Expected: false / Actual: true`; on `origin/main` it passes (ownership established with a `git worktree` of `ac87ab8218`).
- **GREEN** — `CompactionManager.compactSession` (`lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart`) now refuses the empty-region blank fold: when the summary is blank **and** the prepared region had nothing summarizable (`messagesToSummarize` and `turnPrefixMessages` both empty), it throws `CompactionException(code: invalidSession)` instead of appending. The classic attempt fails non-transiently → the local trim finds nothing droppable → the exhaustion terminal reports `onBothRolesFailed` + exactly one failed receipt (`fallback: null`, error identical to the hook error) and keeps the failure verdict — the exact shape the red test demands, with the session file byte-identical.
- Two intermediate shapes were **rejected** because they broke shipped pins (both kept green by the final guard):
  - throwing *before* the summarizer dial broke issue #515's regression pin ("budget expiry must cancel the in-flight summarizer call" — the dial itself must still happen);
  - refusing *every* blank summary broke issue #578's contract (a dialed blank answer over a real region still lands as a record; only the report omits the block).
- The dial, budget, timeout and trim machinery are untouched; the structured engine, the escalation pass and every forced/cap channel keep their behavior (REG-ESC-1 goldens unchanged).
- **Regression pin added** in `test/compaction/compaction_session_test.dart`: *"empty summarizable region + blank answer: refused, history preserved (gh-2044 CI regression)"* — the CI fixture's exact shape (one ~10-token message, `keepRecentTokens: 150`) asserting the `CompactionException` with `invalidSession`, no `CompactionRecord` appended, branch byte-identical.
- CHANGELOG `## Unreleased`: the gh-2044 entry extended with the follow-up red and the refusal rule.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart` — the empty-region blank-fold refusal in `compactSession` (+ pointer comments; the dial/append paths otherwise unchanged).
- `test/compaction/compaction_session_test.dart` — the new regression pin described above.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — gh-2044 `## Unreleased` entry extended.
- (No further code changes: the four previously-resolved threads' fixes were verified in place on this head — `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed test/compaction/structured_escalation_test.dart` exits 0, the `cancelToken: runToken` wiring and the real `judgeCalls` receipts are present.)

No owned-violations table exists to itemize; the red is accounted below as an owned regression of this PR (green on `origin/main`, red on the branch, root cause inside code this PR changed).
- Local SDK note: `dart format --output=none lib/ test/` still lists pre-existing formatter-drift files this PR does not touch (42 files, unchanged from the previous leg's audit) — left untouched deliberately to keep the diff surgical.

### The red (owned)

`test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart` — *"gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict"* asserted `ok == false` and got `true` (both CI jobs and a local repro). Root cause chain — every link inside this PR's scope:

1. This PR's keep-recent decline in `_pickCheckpointRange` (the correct whole-world-fold fix) makes the structured ladder **decline** the fold when the whole visible path fits `keepRecentTokens` — for the fixture (window 100, one ~10-token message) the structured engine does zero LM calls and settles `(ok: false, timedOut: false)`.
2. The factory's residual fall-through (#148 S7/D4) hands the run to the **classic** engine.
3. The classic engine folds an **empty summarizable region**: `generateSummary`'s #729 chunked path plans **zero chunks** and returns `''` without any LM call — `compactSession` used to append that blank summary as a **junk `CompactionRecord`** anyway.
4. Pass 2 then sees "last entry is already a compaction" → the no-work terminal returns `success: true` **unconditionally** — a hollow success while the context is still over the trigger (10 → 37 tokens, endpoint never dialed). gh-1743's failure-verdict contract was flipped into a fake success.

## Approach (TDD)

- **RED** — reproduced locally before touching production code: the failing test exits 1 with `Expected: false / Actual: true`; on `origin/main` it passes (ownership established with a `git worktree` of `ac87ab8218`).

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-11-02:64a39152` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-11-02

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: new test file is not `dart format` clean**

`dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed test/compaction/structured_escalation_test.dart`
exits 1 on this file — the formatter would rewrap ~15 spots, e.g. line 143:

```dart
return (session, _stateFor(await session.buildContextMessages(), contextWindow: 400000));
```

would become:

```dart

  session,
  _stateFor(await session.buildContextMessages(), contextWindow: 400000),
);
```

AGENTS.md's Quality gates section requires "**dart analyze + dart format clean**". The pre-commit
hook normally self-heals this (reformat + re-stage), but the WIP auto-save commits on this branch
evidently bypassed it. `dart analyze` on the changed files is clean; only formatting lags.

Fix is mechanical:

```bash
dart format test/compaction/structured_escalation_test.dart
```

(CI's fast gate does not re-check formatting, so this will not go red — but the next hook run or
a follow-up commit touching this file will reformat it as noise. Please land it formatted.)

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-11-02:db50c590` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-11-02

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the escalation's "no foldable range" contract branch has zero test coverage**

`_runCheckpointEscalationPass` documents this as a first-class outcome (gh-2044 semantic 5):

```dart
if (range == null) {
  // Bounded no-op (gh-2044 semantic 5): nothing foldable below the
  // keep-recent boundary — e.g. an entirely pinned/exempt foldable prefix.
  ...
  emit(after: before, ok: false, error: const CompactionException(
    'checkpoint escalation found no foldable range below the keep-recent boundary'));
  return true;
}
```

None of the 22 new tests drive it — `grep "no foldable range" test/compaction/` finds nothing. The
branch is reachable in-run: when the ordinary checkpoint ladder consumes the **entire** foldable
prefix, the covered records drop out of the projection and the escalation's `_pickCheckpointRange`
finds only pinned records → `null` → it emits a user-visible `ok:false` FAILED receipt while the
run verdict stands. Since this receipt also flows to every host (CLI prints
`auto-compact pass N FAILED ... error=...`), it deserves a pinned test.

Suggested fixture (reuses the UT-ESC-8 style): pin the user ask, judge hides one pair, the ladder
checkpoint folds the remaining unpinned pairs so the settle lands thin with only pinned records
projected; assert exactly one `checkpoint-escalation` pass with `ok == false`, error is a
`CompactionException` mentioning the foldable range, no additional checkpoint appended, and
`run()` still `true`.

Two adjacent untested paths worth covering in the same pass:
- `view == null` at the top of the pass (the `hideableRemaining = 0` diagnostic branch);
- the **factory-level** abort wiring: UT-ESC-9 tests the engine's `cancelToken` directly, but the
  production path is the runToken→budgetSource link (`budgetSource.cancel(runToken.cancelReason)`)
  reaching `_runCancelled` through the reason-type heuristic — no IT test exercises a user abort
  mid-escalation through `AutoCompactorFactory.run()`.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-11-02:5ab747d8` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-11-02

💡 **SUGGESTION: cancellation classification rides a cancel-reason type heuristic — the run token itself is available and never wired**

```dart
bool get _runCancelled {
  if (cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false) return true;
  final source = budgetSource;
  if (source == null) return false;
  return source.token.isCancelled &&
      source.token.cancelReason is! TimeoutException;
}
```

"User abort" is inferred by ruling out `TimeoutException` reasons on the budget token. That holds
for today's callers (I checked: `_activeRun?.source.cancel()` passes no reason, steering cancels
pass strings), but it is a coupling, not a contract: a future caller that cancels the run token
with a `TimeoutException` reason (a watchdog, for example) is silently misclassified as a budget
kill — the escalation then proceeds, its LM call dies instantly, and the abort dissolves into a

Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender's address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.
When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project's file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).

Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host's config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.

## The owner talks to you only

The owner's messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner's address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child's result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content. Video files route to a video-capable model when one is available (the bytes are attached or described with attribution); otherwise a note names how to configure video reading.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the working directory; returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total) as [bash attempt N]; environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — you get the job id immediately and a notice when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed). A command still running after 60s is moved to a background job automatically (never restarted); carried timeouts are NOT auto-retried — retry if the completion notice reports a timeout.

tools.name: bash_job
tools.description: Manage background shell jobs (from bash background: true). Actions: "status" lists running + last 20 exited (all: true = every job; id = one), "output" tails a log (id, lines), "stop" kills a running job (id).

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return ranked results with [n] citation markers, titles, URLs, and snippets. Runs a provider chain (DuckDuckGo first, keyed providers when configured) and falls through on failure. Follow up with web_fetch on a result URL to read the full page.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as Markdown: headings, link anchors, lists, and code blocks are preserved, navigation and boilerplate are stripped. Known sites (pub.dev) are rendered via dedicated handlers. Use it to read pages found with web_search.

tools.name: config
tools.description: Inspect and edit the fa configuration — the user file ~/.fah/config.yaml and the project .fah/config.yaml — without a shell (the same core the `fa config` CLI verbs wrap, available on every host). ops: check = validate both files with the real parsers (errors/warnings/notes + a final ok/failed line); path = list the config file locations and whether each exists; get = the effective value of a dotted key (project scope wins where it participates); set = a surgical single-key write that validates the edited file BEFORE writing, so an invalid value persists nothing. Config keys are documented in the fa-self-config skill — never invent one; unknown keys are rejected. A set result names the file, scope, old -> new value, and whether the change applies live or at next boot.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or past decisions. Use proactively before tasks that might benefit from prior context.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List recent long-term memory entries. Useful to review what the agent already knows.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a stale, wrong, or obsolete entry from long-term memory by id. Prefer deleting over rewriting when the fact no longer holds at all.

tools.name: schedule_message
tools.description: Send a delayed message to an agent mailbox (your own by default) — schedule a follow-up task to check on something later. The message wakes the recipient when it fires; it survives restarts.

tools.name: ask
tools.description:
Ask the user one or more structured questions when you need clarification or a decision during task execution.

<conditions>
- Multiple approaches exist with significantly different tradeoffs the user should weigh
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Use `questions` for multiple related questions instead of asking one at a time
- Use `recommended` (0-based option index or exact option label) to mark the default; the UI badges it as "Recommended"
- Set `multiSelect: true` on a question to allow multiple selections
- Use short option labels; put explanatory tradeoffs in an option's `description` instead of merging them into the label
- Omit `options` when the answer is free-form text
</instruction>

<caution>
- Provide 2-5 concise, distinct options per question
</caution>

<critical>
- **Default to action.** Resolve ambiguity yourself using repo conventions, existing patterns, and reasonable defaults. Exhaust existing sources (code, configs, docs, history) before asking. Only ask when options have materially different tradeoffs the user must decide.
- **If multiple choices are acceptable**, pick the most conservative/standard option and proceed; state the choice.
- **Do NOT include an "Other" option** — the UI always offers free-text input alongside your options.
</critical>

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description:
Ask the user for a credential (API key, token, password) that you need and that is not available yet.

<conditions>
- A command or call fails because a credential is missing, or the task clearly requires one
- The secret is NOT already in the "Available secret env vars" list
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Set `name` to the conventional env var name for the service (GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, NPM_TOKEN...); the user can adjust it before saving
- Explain in `reason` what you need the credential for — the user sees this text
- After the user saves it, reference it as $NAME in shell commands; the value itself never enters the conversation
</instruction>

<critical>
- NEVER ask the user to paste a secret into the chat as plain text — always use this tool, so the value is stored securely and redacted from the transcript
- NEVER print, echo, or write the secret value after it is saved
- If the user declines, do not immediately retry the same request; find another way or explain the blocker
</critical>

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generates an image from a text prompt. Requires the imageGeneration slot to be configured (models.slots.imageGeneration in ~/.fah/config.yaml, or useMainConnection: true to opt into the main connection explicitly). Returns a path to the saved image file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1024x1024"), quality (optional), images (optional, list of reference images: sandbox paths, http(s) URLs, or base64 — supported by OpenRouter image endpoints that accept image input).

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Generates a video from a text prompt. Requires the videoGeneration slot to be configured (models.slots.videoGeneration in ~/.fah/config.yaml, or useMainConnection: true to opt into the main connection explicitly). Returns a path to the saved MP4 file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1920x1080"), quality (optional), images (optional, list of reference images: sandbox paths, http(s) URLs, or base64 — supported by OpenRouter video endpoints that accept image input).

tools.name: decide
tools.description: Ask a structured decision model (OpenRouter Decisions API, e.g. inception/mercury-decide:free) typed questions about a state and receive calibrated answers as structured JSON: yes-no questions come back with a probability, choice questions with the picked option plus per-option probabilities, score questions with a calibrated score over the ordered legend. Requires the main connection to be an OpenRouter provider. Arguments: model (required), state (required — text or JSON), questions (required — object keyed by question name; each entry is {type: bool|choice|score, instructions, criteria} — bool questions ride the Decisions API's `noul` wire type)

tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Check the status of spawned subagents. Without an id, lists ALL subagents with their current state, token usage, and last activity. With an id, shows that subagent in detail.

tools.name: task_observe
tools.description: Read the recent message history of a subagent. Useful to inspect what a child discovered or decided before following up.

tools.name: task_send
tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running child receives it in its inbox at the next turn boundary; an idle (waiting for input) or completed child is resumed in its SAME session with the message. The resume wait is capped (1.5s): a child that does not respond in time reports the message queued and keeps waking in the background (check task_status). Failed children are continued with task_resume instead. Remote a2a:<name> children cannot be steered or resumed — they have no local session or inbox; follow up with a new task item.

tools.name: task_resume
tools.description: Resume a FAILED subagent, continuing the SAME session: the run appends to the existing JSONL transcript, keeps the same mailbox id and display name, and never mints a cloned "name-2" session. Use this after transient failures (provider quota, network). The resume wait is capped (1.5s): a child that does not confirm in time reports the resume continuing in the background — it is never restarted (check task_status). Steering running/idle/completed children is task_send; respawning a fresh agent is task (the new child links supersedes).

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Abort a running background subagent job by id (see task_status for ids). The child agent is cancelled; already-settled jobs report their state instead.

tools.name: reply
tools.description:
Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

REPORT SIZE: per-message budget 8000 chars — you may send one complete reply even when it is larger: the harness auto-spills it (the full text is stored as an agent:// artifact; the parent gets an excerpt + pointer + completeness, and this tool result names the reference). Manual chunking (ordered agent_message parts with report_id + 0-based part_index, more=false on the last, then a final manifest reply carrying report_id + report_parts) is the FALLBACK for when auto-spill is unavailable. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt. Never probe the output limit.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description:
Send a message to another agent: a SIBLING subagent id, "main" for the parent orchestrator (for a final answer prefer reply), an absolute mailbox "<sessionId>/main" to reach another Fa instance sharing this session repo, or "name@machine" to reach a session on another machine (delivered through the A2A gateway; the remote machine must be configured under a2a.servers). A session display NAME from agent_directory works too: "goal_builder" or "goal_builder/main" resolve to that session's live mailbox. The recipient sees the message in its inbox on its next turn; completed siblings are resumed. Unknown ids and full queues are rejected.

REPORT SIZE: budget 8000 chars — oversized same-session bodies auto-spill (stored as an agent:// artifact and delivered as a bounded envelope). Manual chunking (ordered report_id + part_index parts) is the FALLBACK for when auto-spill is unavailable. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt.

tools.name: agent_directory
tools.description: List the agent mailboxes in the messaging fabric that are worth talking to: LIVE mailboxes (registration-backed presence or recent activity), any mailbox holding pending mail, your subagents, and your own address (marked). Each entry shows its session display NAME when known, a short mailbox id, the pending message count, presence ("live" / "busy (run in progress, accepts mail)" / "offline"), the last-activity time for offline entries, and the working directory (home shortened to ~). Declared capabilities render as sub-lines. Stale mailboxes are hidden — pass all: true to list those too (that also shows FULL mailbox ids; the default view truncates them to save tokens). Address a mailbox by its session name via agent_message ("goal_builder", "goal_builder/main", or "name@machine" — a peer on another machine is reachable through the A2A gateway when an a2a.servers entry exists for it); asleep targets are woken with a headless run automatically.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Your session context is limited. Before performing a user request, think whether the work can be delegated to subagents — orchestrate subagents and deliver the result to the user. If it is a simple ask, just perform it yourself.

Run subagents in parallel by passing multiple items in a single `tasks[]` batch. Execution blocks until every item finishes unless `background` is true — then you receive job ids immediately and results deliver as jobs settle.

# Task Design
- **Agent typing:** Pick each item's `agent` type. Read-only research MUST use `agent: "explore"`. Use the default worker only when no specialist fits.
- **No overhead:** Each `task` MUST instruct its subagent to skip formatters, linters, and project-wide test suites. Run those once at the end.
- **One pass:** Prefer subagents that investigate AND edit in one pass; spin a read-only `explore` only when the affected files are genuinely unknown.

# Inputs
- `context`: Shared project state, constraints, and contracts. Applies to the entire batch; do not duplicate this background into individual tasks.
- `tasks[]`: Array of subagents to spawn.
  - `name`: A stable identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), used to address the agent (`agent://` urls, job ids). Uniquified per session; generated from the agent type if omitted.
  - `agent`: The agent type running this item. Omitting it gives you the general-purpose worker (`task`) — NEVER pass that name explicitly. Only omit it after checking the agent list below and finding no specialist that fits.
  - `task`: Complete, self-contained instructions. One-liners or missing acceptance criteria are PROHIBITED.
  - `outputSchema`: Invocation-specific JSON Schema. The subagent's final message must then be a JSON document satisfying it; invalid output gets ONE fix retry, then the item fails.
- `background`: Run items as background jobs (default: host configuration). Blocking calls return every item's output in the result.

# Communication
Subagents start blank — no conversation history. Put everything they need into `context` (shared) and `task` (per item). After spawn, the family stays connected:
- `task_send {id, message}`: steer a running child, answer a waiting (idle) one, or RESUME a completed one with follow-up work.
- `task_resume {id, message?}`: continue a FAILED child in its SAME session — same id, same transcript, same mailbox, never a cloned `name-2` session. Use it after transient failures (provider quota, network); `task_send` is for running/idle/completed children, a fresh `task` for a clean restart (the new child links `supersedes`).
- `task_status` / `task_observe`: inspect the family at any time — status, tokens, and the child's recent transcript.
- Children can `reply` (their explicit answer to you) and `agent_message` (sibling↔sibling hand-offs) — a child that finishes without replying surfaces a `completed_without_reply` notice with its final text preview.
- Completed subagents stay addressable: send them more work instead of re-spawning duplicates.
- Remote `a2a:<name>` children cannot be steered, resumed, or observed — they have no local session. Follow up with a new task item against the same `a2a:<name>` agent.

# Waiting is idle, not blocked
- Long-running children (test suites, builds, research): spawn them with `background: true` and END YOUR TURN right after spawning. Completions and inbox mail wake you automatically, and each result arrives as a message — waiting is an idle state, never a blocked turn.
- NEVER park your turn waiting on children (foreground watch loops, blocking re-polls, sleep-style watchers). A parked turn is unreachable: owner messages queue behind it for as long as the wedge lasts.
- If a blocking call is still running when a user message arrives, the call soft-yields to background — do not re-block afterwards; finish the reply and end the turn.

# Format Contracts
`context` format:
# Goal         ← what the batch accomplishes
# Constraints  ← rules and session decisions
# Contract     ← shared interfaces

`task` format:
# Target       ← exact files and symbols; explicit non-goals
# Change       ← step-by-step add/remove/rename; APIs and patterns
# Acceptance   ← observable result; no project-wide commands

# Results
Each item's full output is addressable as `agent://<id>`. An explicit child `reply` is the deliverable — verbatim within the budget, else a bounded `agent://` envelope (excerpt + pointer + completeness); never a silent stub. Resumed children carry their final answer on the completion notice; a reply acked before a kill survives the resume. For items with an `outputSchema`, the stored output IS the validated JSON object, so typed fields are addressable as `agent://<id>/<dot.path>` (e.g. `agent://Explore/findings.0.path`).

# Report Size
A child report above the per-message budget is never silently truncated: the full redacted text is stored as an `agent://` artifact and the result carries a bounded excerpt, the pointer, and explicit completeness (`complete`/`partial`). Resolve the pointer for the whole report. Chunked reports get a final manifest `reply` the harness validates against the observed parts; missing, duplicated, or out-of-order sets are marked INCOMPLETE.

# Available Agents
### task
General-purpose subagent with full capabilities for delegated multi-step tasks
### explore (READ-ONLY)
Read-only codebase research: rapid analysis, pattern searches, and compressed findings for handoff (uses the smol model role when configured)
### review (READ-ONLY)
Read-only code review specialist for quality and security analysis (uses the slow model role when configured)
### plan (READ-ONLY)
Read-only planning specialist that produces implementation plans without editing code

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description:
Creates a context checkpoint before exploratory work so you can later rewind and keep only a concise report.

Use this when you need to investigate with many intermediate tool calls (read/grep/glob/etc.) and want to minimize context cost afterward.

Rules:
- You MUST call `rewind` before finishing after starting a checkpoint.
- You NEVER call `checkpoint` while another checkpoint is active in the
  same turn. A checkpoint never spans user turns: if one is left unrewound
  when the turn ends, the next `checkpoint` call auto-closes it (the tool
  result names the closed checkpoint) and proceeds.

Typical flow:
1. `checkpoint(goal: …)`
2. Perform exploratory work
3. `rewind(report: …)` with concise findings

After rewind, intermediate checkpoint messages are removed from active context and replaced by the report. The dropped history stays in the session tree; nothing is lost.

tools.name: rewind
tools.description:
End an active checkpoint. Rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.

Call immediately after `checkpoint`-started investigative work.

Requirements:
- `report` MUST be concise, factual, and actionable.
- Include key findings, decisions, and any unresolved risks.
- AVOID raw scratch logs unless essential.
- You MUST call this before finishing if a checkpoint is active.

Behavior:
- If no checkpoint is active, this tool errors. If the checkpoint already rewound, continue from the retained report instead of retrying.
- On success, the session rewinds, keeps your report as retained context, and closes the checkpoint.
- A successful rewind is final for that checkpoint; repeat calls error.

tools.name: compact_expand
tools.description:
Surface and reopen hidden context segments.

Call with NO arguments to list what is hidden: the index of hidden segments with id, kind, size, and a first-line preview each. Pass `query` to filter and rank that index by keyword — it searches the full hidden content, not just previews, so use it when you know WHAT you need but not the id. Discovery is free: it never consumes the expand budget.

To read a segment back, pass its numeric id or range from a marker as `target` (e.g. `5` or `2-6`). Context markers like `[3:hidden·tool_result·4.2k·"first line…"]` or `[2-6:ckpt·38k→40tok·covers:3,5]` are doors, not gravestones: the underlying records stay on disk.

- Giant segments are paged: pass `page` (1-based) to continue past the first page; each page footer states the exact continue call.
- Expanded content counts toward a per-turn budget; every success states the budget left, and when the budget is exhausted the result says so and resets on the next user turn. Only hidden, checkpoint-covered, or summary-folded records expand — the tool tells you when a record is already visible.
- The session file never changes; an expanded segment may be re-hidden later by compaction.

Prefer a targeted expand over re-reading files when the fact was already in context once, and prefer discovery + query over blind ids.

## Managing segments yourself (tier 2)

Pass `action` with a `target` to manage segments directly, without waiting for pressure:

- `action: "hide"` folds a segment you know is dead weight into its expandable marker immediately — one-line marker stays where the content was, `compact_expand` reopens it any time. Real user turns are never hideable; pair groups hide whole; the most recent turns and pinned segments are rejected with the reason.
- `action: "pin"` shields a segment from every hide/compact path (yours, the judge's, pressure-time LRU re-hide); `action: "unpin"` releases it. Pins render on the marker (`·pinned`) and survive session reload.

Hiding and pinning are session state, not edits: the records stay in the file byte-for-byte.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.

guards:
    name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, test-core]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.docs != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app/docs changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.docs == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.docs == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      # gh-1738: activate is its own step so the Quality gates step below
      # can run for docs-only / app-zone-only PRs too — the similarity
      # corpus lives in docs/, prompts/, flutter_app/ and packages/, and
      # a diff confined there must reach the gate pre-merge (it routes
      # away from the CRAP ratchet, which needs the merged lcov).
      - name: Activate crap4dart (pinned)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.docs == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.
          # crap4dart#3/#4 (2026-10-15): >=0.14.2 — the broken_goldens
          # detector fixes (checkmark V, yellow-on-dark digits, hollow
          # boxes, solid glyph runs); the configs now rely on 0.14.2
          # behaviour (severity: error, old excludes dropped).
          # gh-1738: >=0.15.0 — the similarity gate (file-level
          # near-duplicates over md+dart), wired into crap4dart.yaml.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.15.0 <0.16.0"

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # crap4dart activated (pinned) in the step above.
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        # gh-1738: + docs/app — the similarity gate scans the whole tree
        # (docs/, prompts/, flutter_app/, packages/ included); no project
        # pub get needed (global tool, config+file gates only).
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.docs == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline

      # Issue #1234 rework: 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override (a
      # gates.loc.sources key is a ConfigException — caught here on
      # 019ede65), and the package config's sources drive the CRAP census

[test/compaction/structured_escalation_test.dart#06DB]
INS.PRE 1144:
+  group('UT-ESC-13 — an over-window run whose whole ledger fits '
+      'keepRecentTokens still folds (gh-2044 rework, flutter_app '
+      'over-window relief AC)', () {
+    test('the ladder folds the tool-result-heavy whole world when relief is '
+        'required — the decline stays escalation-only', () async {
+      // The flutter_app over-window fixture (agent_service_test.dart
+      // "auto-compaction over-window guard"): user ask + carrier +
+      // a 34000-char tool result over an 8192 window with the app's
+      // hosted settings (reserve 2048, keep 4096). The request estimate
+      // (~8.5k) is far over the trigger, yet every LEDGER token (~870)
+      // fits keepRecentTokens — the keep-recent walk cuts nowhere, and
+      // the tool result alone exceeds the window, so folding the whole
+      // world is the ONLY summarizer-based relief. The shared decline
+      // must NOT starve the ladder here: main's whole-world fold
+      // collapsed this transcript to ~85 tokens and the turn continued;
+      // the decline turned the relief into a hollow classic record
+      // (+29 tokens) and the app AC red.
+      final session = await repo.create(
+        JsonlSessionCreateOptions(cwd: '/work'),
+      );
+      await session.appendMessage(UserMessage.text('go'));
+      await session.appendMessage(_carrier('tc-1'));
+      await session.appendMessage(_result('tc-1', 8500));
+      final model = Model(
+        id: 'm1',
+        name: 'm1',
+        api: 'anthropic-messages',
+        provider: 'p',
+        baseUrl: 'http://localhost:1',
+        contextWindow: 8192,
+        maxTokens: 4096,
+      );
+      final state = _stateFor(
+        await session.buildContextMessages(),
+        contextWindow: 8192,
+      );
+      const appSettings = CompactionSettings(
+        enabled: true,
+        reserveTokens: 2048,
+        keepRecentTokens: 4096,
+      );
+      final before = _requestTokens(state);
+      expect(before, greaterThan(8192 - 512));
+      expect(
+        _settledTokens(await session.getEntries(), {}),
+        lessThan(appSettings.keepRecentTokens),
+        reason: 'fixture precondition: every ledger token fits '
+            'keepRecentTokens — the whole-world regime',
+      );
+
+      final hooks = _CapturingAutoHooks();
+      final ok = await AutoCompactorFactory(
+        session: session,
+        state: state,
+        window: 8192,
+        settings: appSettings,
+        sources: AutoCompactorSources(
+          smolStream: null,
+          smolModel: null,
+          mainStream: (m, c, {cancelToken}) {
+            final message = streamMessage(StopReason.stop, 'continued');
+            return streamOf(message, [DoneEvent(reason: StopReason.stop, message: message)]);
+          },
+          mainModel: model,
+        ),
+        hooks: hooks,
+        prompts: const CompactionPrompts(),
+        engine: CompactionEngine.structured,
+      ).run();
+
+      expect(ok, isTrue);
+      final folds = hooks.passes
+          .where((p) => p.ok && p.tokensAfter < p.tokensBefore)
+          .toList();
+      expect(
+        folds,
+        isNotEmpty,
+        reason: 'relief is required: at least one pass must SHRINK the '
+            'request — the app relief gate reads afterTokens < beforeTokens',
+      );
+      expect(
+        hooks.passes.map((p) => p.fallback),
+        everyElement(startsWith('structured')),
+        reason: 'no hollow classic fall-through may run when the ladder '
+            'can fold',
+      );
+      expect(
+        (await session.getEntries()).whereType<CompactionRecord>(),
+        isEmpty,
+        reason: 'the classic contentless record must not appear',
+      );
+      final after = _requestTokens(
+        _stateFor(await session.buildContextMessages(), contextWindow: 8192),
+      );
+      expect(
+        after,
+        lessThan(before),
+        reason: 'the rebuilt projection must shrink: the huge tool result '
+            'folds into the checkpoint summary',
+      );
+    });
+  });
+
